translation_en: Ibrahim ibn Hamzah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who told him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, wrote to Caesar, inviting him to Islam. He sent the letter to him with Dihyah al-Kalbi. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, instructed him to give it to the governor of Busra, who would then deliver it to Caesar. After Allah had driven the Persian forces away from him, Caesar had walked from Hims to Iliya in gratitude for what Allah had granted him. When the letter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, reached Caesar, he said after reading it, ‘Find someone here from his people so that I may ask them about the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.’ Ibn ‘Abbas said: Abu Sufyan informed me that he was in Syria with some men from Quraysh. They had come there as traders during the truce between the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and the unbelievers of Quraysh. Abu Sufyan said: Caesar’s messenger found us in one part of Syria and took me and my companions with him until we reached Iliya. We were brought in to see Caesar, who was seated in his royal court wearing his crown, with the leading Romans around him. He said to his interpreter, ‘Ask them which of them is closest in kinship to this man who claims to be a prophet.’ Abu Sufyan said: I replied, ‘I am the closest of them in kinship.’ He asked, ‘What is your relationship to him?’ I said, ‘He is my cousin.’ At that time there was no one from Banu ‘Abd Manaf in the travelling party besides me. Caesar said, ‘Bring him closer.’ He ordered my companions to stand behind me, near my shoulders. Then he said to his interpreter, ‘Tell his companions that I will question this man about the one who claims to be a prophet. If he lies, tell me that he is lying.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, had I not felt ashamed that my companions might report a lie from me, I would have lied about him when Caesar questioned me. But I was ashamed that they might report a lie from me, so I told him the truth. Then Caesar said to his interpreter, ‘Ask him: What is this man’s standing among you in terms of lineage?’ I said, ‘He has noble lineage among us.’ He asked, ‘Has anyone among you made this claim before him?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Did you accuse him of lying before he made this claim?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Was any of his forefathers a king?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Do the leading people follow him, or the weak among them?’ I said, ‘Rather, the weak among them.’ He asked, ‘Are they increasing in number or decreasing?’ I said, ‘They are increasing.’ He asked, ‘Does anyone leave his religion out of resentment after entering it?’ I said, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Does he betray?’ I said, ‘No. We are now in a truce with him, though we fear he may betray us.’ Abu Sufyan said: I could not find a way to add anything against him except that, and I was afraid that something else I said might be reported about me. Caesar asked, ‘Have you fought him, or has he fought you?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘How has the war between him and you gone?’ I said, ‘It has been alternating: sometimes we have the upper hand, and sometimes he has the upper hand.’ He asked, ‘What does he command you to do?’ I said, ‘He commands us to worship Allah alone and associate nothing with Him; he forbids us from worshipping what our forefathers worshipped; and he commands us to pray, give charity, be chaste, fulfill our covenants, and return what has been entrusted to us.’ When I had said that, Caesar said to his interpreter, ‘Tell him: I asked you about his lineage among you, and you claimed that he has noble lineage. That is how messengers are sent from among the noblest of their people. I asked whether anyone among you had made this claim before him, and you said no. I said that if anyone among you had made this claim before him, I would have thought that he was following a claim made before him. I asked whether you had accused him of lying before he made his claim, and you said no. I therefore know that he would not stop lying to people and then lie about Allah. I asked whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you said no. I said that if one of his forefathers had been a king, I would have thought that he was seeking his forefathers’ kingdom. I asked whether the leading people or the weak among them follow him, and you said that the weak among them follow him. They are the followers of the messengers. I asked whether they are increasing or decreasing, and you said they are increasing. That is how faith grows until it is complete. I asked whether anyone leaves his religion out of resentment after entering it, and you said no. That is how faith is when its joy enters hearts: no one resents it. I asked whether he betrays, and you said no. That is how the messengers are; they do not betray. I asked whether you fought him and he fought you, and you said that it had happened, and that the war between you and him alternates: sometimes you have the upper hand, and sometimes he has the upper hand. That is how the messengers are: they are tested, and the final outcome is theirs. I asked you what he commands you to do, and you said that he commands you to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, forbids you from worshipping what your forefathers worshipped, and commands you to pray, speak truthfully, be chaste, fulfill your covenants, and return what has been entrusted to you.’ Caesar then said, ‘This is the description of a prophet. I knew that he would appear, but I did not think he would be from among you. If what you have told me is true, he will soon rule the ground beneath these two feet of mine. If I hoped that I could reach him, I would take the trouble to meet him. If I were with him, I would wash his feet.’ Abu Sufyan said: Then Caesar called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and it was read. It said: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the great ruler of the Romans. Peace be upon those who follow guidance. To continue: I invite you with the invitation of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe. Accept Islam, and Allah will give you your reward twice over. If you turn away, the sin of the Erisiyyin will be upon you. “People of the Scripture, come to a word that is fair between us and you: that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him, and that none of us take others as lords besides Allah. If they turn away, then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims’” (3:64).’ Abu Sufyan said: When Caesar had finished speaking, the voices of the leading Romans around him rose, and their noise grew loud. I do not know what they said. We were ordered out and taken away. When I had left with my companions and was alone with them, I said, ‘The affair of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become great. Even the king of Banu al-Asfar fears him.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, I remained humiliated and certain that his cause would prevail until Allah placed Islam in my heart, though I disliked it.
